checklist.item: Queries. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for every query on the request path and at startup. Flag every full table scan (SCAN) and every temporary B-tree (USE TEMP B-TREE) over results.
checklist.evidence: A bun:sqlite preload recorded every SQL text that ran while the API (1x bench seed, 20 bench checks, a heartbeat check, 2 components, 1 maintenance window) started, ran retention, the latency backfill and heartbeat ticks, and answered one request to every documented route: POST /results with an incident opened and resolved, every public GET and variant, /probe/checks, heartbeat, admin config writes with a hot reload, and every manual-incident write; all 2xx. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN of all 51 DML statements on the same database (SQLite 3.53.2), exit 0. No SCAN of results; every results read is a SEARCH on results_by_check, results_by_sample or results_by_time. Temporary B-trees over results: dayLatencies ORDER BY latency_ms (src/service.ts:521; GET /latency, GET /checks/:id/latency, backfill) and dailyUptime GROUP BY day (src/service.ts:515; GET /uptime, /checks, /components, /components/uptime). SCAN incidents + USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY in all 5 listIncidents variants (src/service.ts:1099; GET /incidents, GET /components) and SCAN i in openInactive (startup and config loads). SCAN manual_incidents + TEMP B-TREE (src/manual-incidents.ts:103-108). SCAN checks in 8 statements (bounded by the configured checks). SCAN latency_daily and manual_incidents in retention deletes. SCAN locs + TEMP B-TREE FOR GROUP BY over (check, location) pairs in NEWEST_PER_LOCATION_SQL at startup. SCAN sqlite_master LIMIT 1 in migrate. Measured in item 3: findings 2, 3 and 4.

checklist.item: Startup. A CPU profile of the startup (bun --cpu-prof), with the top functions by self time.
checklist.evidence: Bench A/B startup_cpu_ms: B (main) 205 ms (210, 200), A (baseline 8ea397c) 540 ms; budget 325 ms, ok; nightly c282ae3 240 ms. Local CPU at the first 200 of /readyz without the profiler: 120, 110 and 100 ms (1x). bun --cpu-prof --cpu-prof-interval=100 src/main.ts, SIGTERM at the first 200 of /readyz, 3 runs per data size, exit 0: CPU at ready 150/140/140 ms (1x) and 140/130/140 ms (10x), so startup does not grow with the data. Top self time over the 3 runs at 1x (392.7 ms sampled): node:fs module 40.4 ms (10.3 %), native bun:sqlite run (openDb/migrate BEGIN IMMEDIATE, schema, COMMIT, PRAGMAs) 37.9 ms (9.6 %), _onceWrap node:events 22.3 ms (5.7 %), setName node:fs 18.9 ms (4.8 %), startLatencyRollup src/latency-rollup.ts:60 16.8 ms (4.3 %), isServerConfig bun:main 14.6 ms (3.7 %), native code under node:_http_client 10.0 ms and under node:http 8.8 ms, zod schema construction 6.2 + 5.5 ms, DurationFormat 5.4 ms. 10x: bun:sqlite run 46.6 ms (11.9 %) on top, then module loading. Bench startup_wall_ms 1434 ms is over its reported budget of 618 ms; without Docker the API is ready 85-153 ms after the spawn (note). No finding.

checklist.item: Costs that grow with data. The repository's bench, or a local A/B with a larger data set (for example 10x the bench seed). Report how each measured cost changes with the data size.
checklist.evidence: Bench A/B (A 8ea397c, B main, 2 rounds): every api gating metric ok; p95_get_latency_ms 129 ms and p95_get_check_latency_ms 127 ms are over the reported budgets 53 and 55 ms on A and B; their cause is not established (the review measured 19-24 ms at the same rates without Docker; see review.removedFindings). Local growth script: fresh copy of the seeded database per run, start, wait for the backfill, then 30 x (POST /results; timed GET route) per route; 3 runs per data set; exit 0. Medians at 1x / 10x (8.64 M rows) / end-of-day density contiguous / end-of-day interleaved (25,920 results per check today, as 3 locations at 10 s give in a full day): GET /checks 3.1 / 18.6 / 195.5 / 344.7 ms; GET /uptime 2.6 / 17.9 / 193.9 / 341.4 ms; GET /latency 3.8 / 26.2 / 266.3 / 424.0 ms; GET /components/uptime 2.4 / 17.7 / 194.0 / 341.0 ms; GET /checks/c0/latency 0.4 / 1.4 / 13.2 ms; GET /components 2.5 / 17.8 / 194.1 ms; GET /checks/c0/results 0.3 / 0.3 / 0.3 ms. First (cold) GET /checks after start 206.7 / 2,354.4 / 455.2 / 608-612 ms; first GET /uptime 211.0 / 2,412.2 / 461.8 / 615-619 ms. Latency backfill (1780 days) CPU about 0.78 s at 1x and 3.6 s at 10x, with a yield per (check, day). Startup CPU and RSS do not grow (RSS at ready 60 MiB at 1x and 10x). 1x + 100,000 incidents: /incidents?status=resolved 0.2 to 8.2 ms, ?status=open 0.2 to 3.7 ms, /components 2.5 to 6.5 ms. Read routes grow linearly with today's results (finding 2), first reads with the 30/90-day history (finding 3), incident reads with all incidents (finding 4).

Budgets idle_rss_mib 88 and peak_rss_mib 115 MiB: within; bench B 75.38 and 99.90 MiB. No finding.

PULSE_CHECKS_FILE=... PULSE_TOKENS_FILE=... bun src/main.ts; after 'backfill done', 30 x (curl -X POST /results; curl -w '%{time_total}' GET <route>) per route; 3 server runs

removedFindings.title: Each ingest commits with a synchronous disk flush on the event loop; every route's p95 is about 180-250 ms at the bench rates
removedFindings.reason: Not reproduced. At the bench rates the database on disk and on tmpfs give almost the same latencies, and every route stays far within its budget. The flush per ingest exists (4 fsync and 1 journal unlink per commit), but costs about 1 ms per POST on this disk.
removedFindings.command: timeout 200 bun load.ts <api copy> <db> <seed dir> <port> 60 (bun src/main.ts on a copy of the 1x bench seed; after 'backfill done', 60 s open loop at the bench/load.ts rates: 30 POST /results, 10 GET /checks, 1 GET /uptime, 1 GET /latency, 1 GET /checks/c0/latency per second); disk twice, tmpfs (/dev/shm) once, disk with a parallel 6 GB dd once; plus a 20 s run under strace -f -c -e trace=fsync,fdatasync,unlink,unlinkat
removedFindings.excerpt:
PRAGMA synchronous 2, journal_mode delete
disk 1: POST /results p50 2.0 p95 2.9 ms | GET /checks p95 9.0 | GET /latency p95 23.2 | GET /checks/c0/latency p95 23.9 ms
disk 2: POST /results p50 2.1 p95 3.2 ms | GET /checks p95 9.9 | GET /latency p95 19.5 | GET /checks/c0/latency p95 20.0 ms
tmpfs:  POST /results p50 1.0 p95 1.2 ms | GET /checks p95 7.8 | GET /latency p95 19.2 | GET /checks/c0/latency p95 19.8 ms

removedFindings.note: The cost depends on the fsync latency of the disk; this review cannot show it as a finding on a disk with a slow flush. The bench A/B p95_get_latency_ms 129 ms and p95_get_check_latency_ms 127 ms (over budget on A and B) stay in bench.localAB; their cause in the Docker bench stack is not established.
